# Independent scientific challenge: public-plan containment under roster churn

Please act as an independent scientific innovator and adversarial mathematical
reviewer. I am studying a narrow causal-identification question in multi-agent
roster churn, not asking for code review and not asking whether a particular
forced reset is bad.

Consider a finite post-event control problem in which the entire physical
state and history are public. At the membership event, every controller sees
the unordered active roster, survivor/newcomer/departure status, positions and
resources, current public targets and demand, the pre-event public plan and
assignment, all earlier public roster and plan events, deterministic public tie
rules, the future exogenous dynamics law, and the same observation, action,
service, and decision clocks. There is no hidden plan, private setup state,
undisclosed event, or arm-specific history.

The CARRY continuation retains all still-legal public claims. When churn makes
literal preservation infeasible, it uses a fully specified public repair:
first maximize the number of survivor claims retained, then minimize total
physical travel, then apply a public lexicographic tie rule. Every later action
of this continuation is part of the CARRY policy.

The public REPLAN class has the same information, future law, objective,
actions, horizon, dynamics, clocks, and randomization. It contains the complete
CARRY continuation for every legal public history and also contains at least
one genuinely different legal policy. There is no limit on computation,
optimization, data, parameters, search, or inference latency. A competent
selector minimizes the same physical objective over the REPLAN class. Physical
loss is the lexicographic pair of recovery time and integrated normalized
unserved demand; I also care about the full Pareto-minimal endpoint set so that
an arbitrary scalarization cannot decide the answer.

The central question is whether CARRY can ever have direct physical recovery
or nonharm value over that competent containing class. The obvious inclusion
argument says that the REPLAN attainable set contains the exact CARRY
trajectory distribution, so an optimal REPLAN can copy CARRY or do better. I
want you to try hard to break that argument rather than merely restating it.

Please do four things. First, formulate the strongest correct containment
theorem you can for finite-horizon stochastic public-history policies and joint
multi-agent actions. State the quantifiers carefully, including whether the
claim is about a policy class, an optimal selector, every endpoint-optimal
policy, or the existence of one REPLAN policy that matches CARRY. Cover public
common randomness, path-dependent histories, churn-forced repair, vector
endpoints, and both roster expansion and contraction.

Second, give the precise assumptions on information, policy membership,
actions, dynamics, objective, risk or tie selection, and useful computation
that make the theorem true. Identify every meaningful failure condition you
can. Separate genuine mathematical failures from cases that simply remove
CARRY from the class, hide its plan from REPLAN, force a reset, weaken the
selector, change the objective, restrict decentralized coordination, or impose
a finite learning/search budget. Those are important boundaries, but they do
not count as a same-information physical counterexample.

Third, search constructively for a finite counterexample that preserves all of
the stated matching and true functional containment. A valid example would
need churn to force at least one nonzero survivor reassignment, yet no competent
endpoint-optimal REPLAN could select CARRY or the same maximum-overlap/minimum-
travel repair even though that continuation remains a legal member of the
class. If you think such an example exists, specify the complete public state,
event, legal joint actions, transition and service law, objective, CARRY repair,
REPLAN class, and exact endpoint-optimal policy set. Explain how it avoids the
set-inclusion argument. If no example can exist, give a concise impossibility
proof and explain why finite enumeration would be redundant.

Fourth, advise what smallest next discriminator would actually change the
scientific decision. The current physical-only claim must exclude finite-budget
optimization, partial observability, private setup state, changed objectives,
and forced replan conventions. If the theorem is airtight under those
exclusions, say whether the scientifically honest conclusion is to narrow RCLE
to one of those different future objects rather than spend on another public
physical host. Preserve a finite claim ceiling: do not infer anything about
latent necessity, learned regularization, arbitrary roster processes, UAV
transfer, safety, or deployment.

Return a self-contained scientific answer. Lead with either the theorem and
its exact boundary or a concrete valid counterexample. Make the strongest
